summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments by triaging, implementing fixes, and replying to/resolving each thread.
summary.outcome: Two valid fixes were implemented (core package.json version bump and FolderTree key material cloning), one comment was dismissed as not applicable (orval-generated artifact), all 53 tests pass, and changes were committed and pushed.

repo: packages/api-client contains mostly orval-generated code — coverage thresholds were set to 0% and generated directories excluded from coverage
FolderTree previously zeroed caller-provided key buffers on insert rather than cloning them first, which was a security/correctness issue
teeKeysDtoPreviousPublicKey.ts is an orval-generated artifact; parent type correctness makes direct suggestions not applicable

code.finding: Key material passed by callers must be cloned on insert, not zeroed in place — callers still hold references to those buffers
Test was asserting that caller buffers got zeroed after insert; had to be updated to reflect the new clone-on-insert contract
Package version was incorrect and required a fix per review comment

workflow: Use GraphQL reviewThreads query to fetch unresolved PR threads; REST API does not expose thread resolution status cleanly
Reply to threads via REST (gh api with --field for integer in_reply_to) and resolve via GraphQL mutation separately — these are two distinct API calls
Run full test suite before committing even when fixes seem small — the FolderTree change required a corresponding test update

friction: Existing test for FolderTree was coupled to the old (incorrect) behavior of zeroing caller buffers, requiring a test fix alongside the production fix
open_items: api-client package has 0% coverage thresholds and passWithNoTests — should revisit whether any non-generated logic needs tests added
orval-generated files are excluded from coverage but may drift from API spec; no automated check for that currently
